Rashi on Shabbat 77b:10:1.hebrew: כופתא - מכתשת. ל"א: מדה לחטין. ול"נ: כמין גולם עץ עשוי לישיבה, כמו כופת שאור שיחדה לישיבה, דתניא בפסחים (דף מה:):
Rashi on Shabbat 77b:10:1.english: Kufta - A mortar. Another explanation: A measure for wheat. And it seems to me [that it is] a sort of wooden block made for sitting, like “a block of sourdough that one designated for sitting,” as it is taught in Pesachim (45b).

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:10:10.english: Meshikhla - A large basin from which everyone washes their hands and feet.

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:10:13.hebrew: משיא כלתא - מיוחד לחשובים, כמו כלה ואשה חשובה, לרחוץ ממנו:
Rashi on Shabbat 77b:10:13.english: Washes the bride - [The vessel] is designated for distinguished people, such as a bride or an important woman, to wash from it.

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:10:15.english: Chasirta [lacking] - For it is lacking [material due to] the carving on the inside.

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:10:16.english: Bukhna - A pestle with which they pound.

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:10:2.english: Turn [it] over, sit - Invert it and sit upon it.

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:10:3.english: For the children of the children of [one's] children - It endures for many generations.

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:10:4.english: Hutza - A fence of thorns or palm branches.

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:10:5.hebrew: חציצה - אינו דבר קיימא, אלא חציצה בעלמא:
Rashi on Shabbat 77b:10:5.english: A partition - It is not a permanent thing, but merely a partition.

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:10:7.hebrew: כזה - כלומר, דבר מועט וקל כמו זהו — מהו חשוב למלאותו לי מיינך במתנה:
Rashi on Shabbat 77b:10:7.english: Like this - That is to say, [one says: “It is] a small and slight thing like this — how significant is it to fill it for me from your wine as a gift?”

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:10:8.english: Shutita - A branch of myrtle with which they dance before a bride.

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:10:9.english: Madness - The one who dances appears like a madman.

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:11:1.english: Levusha - An outer tunic, which they call sarroc [in Old French].

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:11:10.hebrew: אפתחא - אל פתח זה יבאו הכל — אם למשפט, אם לשרת המלך:
Rashi on Shabbat 77b:11:10.english: To the entrance - To this entrance all will come, whether for judgment or to serve the king.

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:11:2.hebrew: לא בושה - למנוע הבושה, שמכסה כל החלוקים התחתונים הקרועים ורעים:
Rashi on Shabbat 77b:11:2.english: No shame - To prevent shame, as it covers all the undergarments that are torn and shabby.

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:11:3.english: Like a golem - Which has no distinct limbs.

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:11:5.hebrew: גלי ותיב - כשהוא יושב מגלה עצמו, שלא ישב עליו, שלא ילכלכנו, ולא ישופנו בקרקע וישיר שערו, ויקרע ויבלה:
Rashi on Shabbat 77b:11:5.english: Uncover and sit - When he sits, he uncovers himself, so that he does not sit on it, so that he does not dirty it, and does not rub it against the ground and [thereby] shed its nap, and [lest it] tear and wear out.

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:11:6.english: Bor zinka - A pit whose water has dried up, they call [it] so.

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:11:8.english: A scarf - It is the practice of Torah scholars to wrap [themselves in] a scarf.

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:12:1.english: A small limb - One of the joints of the little finger.

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:12:2.hebrew: דגדול - של אדם גדול, והאי קטן אאבר קאי. אי נמי: אבר גדול של קטן, והאי קטן אגברא קאי ולא אאבר:
Rashi on Shabbat 77b:12:2.english: Of an adult - Of an adult person, and this [word] "small" refers to the limb; or alternatively: a large limb of a child, and this [word] "small" refers to the person and not to the limb.

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:12:3.hebrew: לא אבר קטן - וקטן אכולא מילתא קאי — אבר קטן של גוף קטן:
Rashi on Shabbat 77b:12:3.english: No, a small limb - And [the word] “small” applies to the entire matter — a small limb of a small body.

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:13:1.hebrew: דרבי שמעון כו' - והכי קאמר: כדי לסוך בו אבר קטן, וקטן יהא הגוף — בן יומו. ורבי נתן סבר: חד קטן אמרינן — או האבר או הגוף, אבל תרי קוטני — לא:
Rashi on Shabbat 77b:13:1.english: That Rabbi Shimon, etc. - And this is what it means: Enough to anoint with it a small limb, and the body shall be small — a day-old [child]. And Rabbi Natan holds: We say [only] one "small" — either the limb or the body, but two "smalls" — no.

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:13:2.hebrew: ה"ג - דכולי עלמא אבר קטן של קטן בן יומו — לא:
Rashi on Shabbat 77b:13:2.english: This is the correct reading: Everyone agrees that [for] a small limb of a day-old child, [one is] not [liable].

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:1:1.hebrew: גראינין - מתניתין דפרקין דלעיל: "חוץ מקליפתן וגרעיניהן":
Rashi on Shabbat 77b:1:1.english: Gar’inin - [This refers to] the Mishnah of our preceding chapter: “Except for their peels and their seeds.”

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:1:2.hebrew: ונגרע - והגרעינין זורקין, ונגרעין מתוך האוכל:
Rashi on Shabbat 77b:1:2.english: “And it shall be subtracted” - And the seeds, one throws [them] away, and they are subtracted from the food.

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:2:1.hebrew: אוממות - גבי גחלים מייתינן ליה בכיצד צולין: "גחלים, יכול עוממות? ת"ל 'אש'. אי 'אש', יכול שלהבת..." כו':
Rashi on Shabbat 77b:2:1.english: Omemot [dimming coals] - Regarding coals, we cite it in [the chapter] Keitzad Tzolin: "[Since the verse states] 'coals,' [one] might [think] dimming [coals]? The verse states: 'Fire.' If 'fire,' [one] might [think] a flame?..." etc.

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:2:2.english: Obscured it - [They] did not darken its appearance by being more beautiful than it.

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:3:1.hebrew: מאמצין - לקמן, גבי עינים של מת, בפ' שואל (שבת דף קנא:):
Rashi on Shabbat 77b:3:1.english: Me’amtzin - Later, regarding the eyes of the dead, in the chapter [entitled] Shoel (Shabbat 151b).

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:4:1.english: In a rubbing of collyrium - For they are accustomed to rub it with a woman's milk.

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:4:2.english: Sufficient to rub with water - For two eyes.

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:4:3.hebrew: כדי שיפה או כדי אחיזה ושיפה - מה שנדבק באצבעותיו, לבד מה שנותן בעיניו:
Rashi on Shabbat 77b:4:3.english: Enough for rubbing, or enough for holding and rubbing - That which sticks to his fingers, in addition to what he puts in his eyes.

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:5:1.english: On the mouth of the entire sore - And every wound is called a “mouth.”

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:5:2.english: The primary protuberance - The uppermost [part] of the wound.

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:6:1.english: A snail - *Limace* [Old French for a slug].

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:6:2.english: For a sore - One places it [the snail] upon it [the sore].

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:6:3.hebrew: זבוב לצירעה - למי שעקצו צירעה, כותש זבוב ומניחה עליו:
Rashi on Shabbat 77b:6:3.english: A fly for a wasp - For one whom a wasp stung, he crushes a fly and places it upon him.

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:6:5.english: Semamit - Ireinie [iraigne, a spider] in the Old French vernacular.

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:6:6.hebrew: לעקרב - עקיצת עקרב, כותש סממית ומניחה עליו:
Rashi on Shabbat 77b:6:6.english: For a scorpion - [For] a scorpion's sting, one crushes a spider and places it upon it.

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:7:1.hebrew: מפגיע - חיה קטנה וקולה גדול, ושומע וירא שתהא בריה גדולה, ובורח:
Rashi on Shabbat 77b:7:1.english: Mafgia - A small animal whose voice is loud; and [the lion] hears [it] and fears that it may be a large creature, and flees.

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:7:2.hebrew: יתוש - נכנס לפיל בחוטמו, וכן סממית לעקרב — נכנס לו באזנו:
Rashi on Shabbat 77b:7:2.english: Mosquito - It enters the elephant's trunk; and similarly, a gecko to a scorpion — it enters its ear.

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:7:3.hebrew: סנונית - ארונדייל"א, נכנסת תחת כנפי הנשר ומעכבו מפרישת כנפיו:
Rashi on Shabbat 77b:7:3.english: Swallow - *Arondele* [Old French for swallow]; it enters under the wings of the eagle and prevents it from spreading its wings.

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:7:4.hebrew: כילבית - שרץ קטן, ונכנס לדג גדול באזנו:
Rashi on Shabbat 77b:7:4.english: Kilbit - A small creature, and it enters into a large fish through its ear.

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:7:5.english: “He that causes destruction to flash upon the mighty” - He Who strengthens the plundered over the mighty.

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:8:1.hebrew: כל חללי עלמא - פירוש: דברים הנעשים בכל חלל העולם:
Rashi on Shabbat 77b:8:1.english: All the spaces of the world - Meaning: Matters that occur throughout the expanse of the world.

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:8:2.english: [They] walk at the head of the flock - They walk at the head of the flock.

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:8:3.hebrew: ברישא חשוכא - סתם עזים שחורות, סתם רחלות לבנות:
Rashi on Shabbat 77b:8:3.english: At first [there was] darkness - Goats are typically black, [and] ewes are typically white.

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:8:5.english: And these are exposed - The goats do not have a fat tail.

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:8:6.hebrew: הני דמכסינן מינייהו - רחלים, שאנחנו מתכסין מצמרן, גם הן מכוסות:
Rashi on Shabbat 77b:8:6.english: These that we cover ourselves from - Ewes: since we cover ourselves with their wool, they too are covered.

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:8:7.hebrew: דאכלה כיסי - קוצים. לפיכך זנבו קצר, כדי שלא ידבקו בה הקוצים:
Rashi on Shabbat 77b:8:7.english: Because it eats thorns [kisei] - [Meaning] thorns. Therefore, its tail is short, so that thorns will not stick to it.

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:8:8.english: And needs to fend off mosquitoes - To drive away the mosquitoes.

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:9:1.english: A grasshopper - A locust. And it seems to me [that] kamtsa [is an ant].

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:9:3.hebrew: ואי קשיא נדיא ומתעוורא - ואם היתה קשה, תנוד ותעקר כשתכה בעצים:
Rashi on Shabbat 77b:9:3.english: And if [it were] hard, it would be dislodged and go blind - And if it were hard, it would be shaken and uprooted when it strikes against the trees.

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:9:4.hebrew: ומתעוורא - יסתמו עיניה, שמראות עיניה תלויה בה, כדשמואל:
Rashi on Shabbat 77b:9:4.english: And it would go blind - Its eyes will be blinded, for its eyesight is dependent on it, as [stated by] Shmuel:

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:9:5.hebrew: תימרא דתרנגולא מידליא לעילא - ריס של עין התחתון — כשעוצם עיניו, עולה למעלה מן העליון; ובשאר כל בריה, העליון שוכב על התחתון:
Rashi on Shabbat 77b:9:5.english: The eyelid of a chicken rises upward - The lower eyelid — when it closes its eyes, it rises above the upper one, whereas in all other creatures, the upper one lies upon the lower one.

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:9:6.hebrew: משום דדייר אדפי - שעולה בלילות על הקרשים והקורות, צריך שיעלה התחתון על העליון, מפני העשן שלא יכנס בעיניו:
Rashi on Shabbat 77b:9:6.english: Because it lives on rafters - Since it goes up at night onto the boards and the beams, it needs the lower [eyelid] to rise over the upper [one] on account of the smoke, so that it does not enter its eyes.

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:9:7.hebrew: מתכוליתא - דבר שמטבילין בו, כגון כותח או שאר ליפתן:
Rashi on Shabbat 77b:9:7.english: Matkulita - Something in which one dips [bread], such as kutach or other relish.

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:9:8.hebrew: מתי תכלה דא - לכשיכלה, מה נאכל? ול"נ: מתי תכלה דא — לפי שאינו כלה עד זמן ארוך, שאינו נאכל אלא מעט מעט:
Rashi on Shabbat 77b:9:8.english: When will this be finished - [Meaning,] when it finishes, what will we eat? And it seems to me: [it is called] “When will this be finished?” because it is not finished until a long time [has passed], as it is eaten only little by little.

Rashi on Shabbat 77b:9:9.english: Beita [is] bo ve’eitiv [come and sit] - For it is customary to sit in a house.

Tosafot on Shabbat 77b:13:1.hebrew: דרבי שמעון בן אלעזר סבר אבר קטן של קטן בן יומו כו' - תימה, דאדרבה, איפכא מסתברא: דר' נתן, דקאמר "אבר קטן", משמע טפי של קטן בן יומו מרשב"א, דאמר "אבר קטן וקטן בן יומו"; דהא לעיל פריך ארבי ינאי — דמפרש "אבר קטן" דמתניתין "אבר קטן של קטן בן יומו", דהוי כלישנא דר' נתן — מברייתא דקתני בה כלישנא דרשב"א. ויש לומר: דלמאי דמשני, הוי סברא איפכא, ונקט הכא כדמסיק לעיל. ואית ספרים דגרסי איפכא, ואין נראה — דהא מסיק דלרשב"א אבר קטן של קטן בן יומו, ולמאי דגרס איפכא לא הוי כמסקנא: לא לפי דמייתי השתא, ולא לפי מה שדוחה "לא, דכולי עלמא כו'":
Tosafot on Shabbat 77b:13:1.english: "That Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar holds: A small limb of a day-old child, etc." - [This is] astonishing, for on the contrary, the opposite seems reasonable: that [for] Rabbi Natan, who says "a small limb," it implies even more so [that it means] of a day-old child than Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar, who says "a small limb and a day-old child"! For above, [the Gemara] raised an objection against Rabbi Yannai — who explained "a small limb" of our Mishnah [to mean] "a small limb of a day-old child," which is like the wording of Rabbi Natan — from the baraita that teaches like the wording of Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar. And one can say that according to what [the Gemara] answered, the reasoning became the opposite, and here it formulated [the question] according to what was concluded above. And there are books that have the reverse reading, but it does not appear [correct], for [the Gemara] concludes that according to Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar, [the measure is] a small limb of a day-old child; and according to the one who reads the reverse, it would not match the conclusion — neither according to what it brings now, nor according to what it rejects: "No, everyone [agrees that for a small limb of a day-old child, no] etc."
